data.title: Export / save / copy-css with a live float: stamp it first?

data.body:
Raised by the PM-7 review (see PM-7's review comment for the full reasoning). PM-7 added a floating paste that is deliberately NOT part of the document until stamped (it never bumps dirtyDoc, it is never in history). Every context change stamps it first — tool switch, mode switch, cell size, focus enter/exit/move — EXCEPT the three export escapes in src/main.ts: doSave (pattern.json), doExportPng, doCopyCss. Export mid-paste therefore omits what is on screen.

Coherent as designed, so this is a product call, not a bug: should an explicit export/save stamp the float first (one line each: commitFloatFirst() at the top of the three functions), or keep ignoring it? Needs a human decision on which is less surprising.

Deliberately out of scope either way: autosave. It must NOT stamp — firing a document mutation from a debounced timer the user never triggered is worse than the gap.

Human decision (forrest): current behavior is correct as-is — export/save/copy-css do not stamp a live floating paste; the float is not part of the document until deliberately stamped, and all context changes already stamp first. No code change. Closing.

Human reversed the earlier keep-as-is decision: fix it. Scope per the PM-7 reviewer's analysis: doSave / doExportPng / doCopyCss stamp a live float first (explicit user actions export what's on screen); autosave deliberately does NOT stamp (a debounced timer must never mutate the document).

Implemented by orchestrator: commitFloatFirst() added at the top of doSave/doCopyCss/doExportPng (three one-line calls to the existing helper used by every context change). Autosave subscriber untouched. tsc+build clean.

Reviewed commit faa3440 cold against the plan. Verified: (1) doSave/doCopyCss/doExportPng each call commitFloatFirst() as their first statement, before store.get()/activeBuffer(doc)/downloadProject read any state; (2) commitFloatFirst is a strict no-op without a float (guarded at both call site and inside stampFloatAction), so the no-float path is byte-identical to before; (3) stampFloatAction pushes exactly one history entry and bumps dirtyDoc+dirtyPreview via bumpDoc, so previews and autosave refresh after the stamp; (4) autosave subscriber (lines 762-777) does not stamp — unchanged; (5) src/main.ts diff is exactly three call lines with comments, nothing else. Ordering traced: stampFloat is a synchronous pixel loop (selection.ts:79), so the doc is mutated before doCopyCss/doExportPng read exportScale and activeBuffer — stamped pixels are included in the upscaled buffer and PNG; in doSave the stamp precedes downloadProject serialization. Nothing async races the reads. Tip ordering: 'stamped' is set synchronously, then each action's own store.set (or the copyText .then for css) runs after and wins — the user-visible tip is the export's ('pattern.json' / 'css copied' / 'pattern.png'), correct. stampFloatAction stamps in the same s.mode the export reads. npx tsc --noEmit and npm run build both clean. No findings; meets all acceptance criteria. Verdict: pass, moving to done.
